legendary.why: the owner's decision (kyogre.decision). It fits the place: the station looks east over open sea (data/regions.json marine water off marsh country), and the ocean is 56% of the world (STRUCTURE_DECISIONS.md section 4's Lugia row).
legendary.what_the_station_is: A LEAD, NOT AN ENCOUNTER. The researchers study a sealed dive arch on the sea floor (portal) and the sea's legend. The station gives nothing, sets no state but each researcher's dialogue cursor, and never promises that Kyogre can be met: there is no Kyogre cave, trigger or spawn anywhere in the repository. The arch's destination is a stub (portal.hook).
legendary.why_no_cave_here: the owner's own words put the cave LATER ('will later tp the player to a kyogre cave'). A cave is a legendary site: data/legendaries.json (trigger, tier ceiling, spawn-free zone, chamber builder) and its own audit, and data/portals.json's pocket dimension or a carved chamber for the room.

ground_rule: Every Y is computed by tools/coldwater_station.py from tools/ground.py (the canonical heightmap, rounded). Nothing in this file is a Y. Each piece is seated on max(ground under its footprint) + 1, with a foundation down to the ground under any lower column (tools/frostpeak_camp.py's seat(), CALLED, not copied).

site.measured: 2026-10-05 from tools/ground.py and tools/water_mask.py's rule (sea where the ground is below y62). The site is a NE-facing slope down to the sea: at z1843 the ground is y70 at x6020, y67-68 at x6038-6050, y64 at x6062 and y62 (dry, level with the sea) at x6074; the shelf east of it is shallow, 1 deep for ~10 blocks, 2 deep from ~x6090, 3 deep from ~x6105. Going west the moor climbs to y91 at x5900. Nothing in any other data/*.json lies within 450 blocks except two data/regions.json polygon vertices (32 and 57 blocks; boundaries, not things); the nearest route path is ~1200 blocks off (data/route_paths.json). Rechecked by the tool's guards on every build (rules).

rules.authored_clearance_why: every written column at least this far from any x/z another data/*.json authors (tools/southern_residents.py authored_points, the far south's guard), this file's own ferry dock excepted by id
rules.dock_clearance_why: every station column at least this far from the station jetty's keep-clear box and from its ferryman's and landing's columns (data/ferries.json coldwater_station_jetty)
rules.max_piece_relief: each kind's own (tools/frostpeak_camp.py Piece.relief), and the cabin's 2

arch_buoy.source: portal.site.at and the sea's level (data/world.json vertical.sea_level): the buoy's lantern, one above the float block that replaces the top water layer over the arch's centre column
arch_buoy.aim: the lantern's centre; the line from the telescope must clear every ground block (tools/frostpeak_camp.py clear_above, exact) or the build is refused

landing.source: data/ferries.json docks[id=northlight_landing].ferryman.at, the packet master's spot at Northlight on South Pine Isle
landing.aim: his head height (at y + 1.6). Not required to be visible: the theodolite gives the boat's bearing

portal.status: SEALED: built, clickable and dive-gated like every dive portal; its destination is a stub. Generated by tools/coldwater_station.py (cobblers:coldwater_station/portal/build), NOT by tools/portals.py.
portal.why_not_in_portals_json: tools/portals.py cannot hold an inactive portal cleanly: its load() refuses any gate whose portal count is not a multiple of rules.meaningful_per (6) with one vault in each six (the owner's 1-in-6 rule), rooms are indexed per gate on that count, and every portal there crosses into a built room in cobblers:pocket. A seventh dive portal fails the first rule and a sealed one has no room. So the arch is built by this pack with portals.py's own functions CALLED (world_blocks, apron_columns, clearances, commands, summon, click_advancement) and its data read (blocks.dive, rules, gates.dive).
portal.site_measured: 2026-10-05 from tools/ground.py: the 5 x 5 apron x6189-6193, z1842-1846 is flat at y53 (relief 0), 9 under the sea's y62; the lintel tops out at y57, 5 under the surface (data/portals.json rules: min_submersion 6, min_water_above 3, max_relief 2). The nearest flat floor at least 9 deep on the ferry lane: the shelf off the deck is 1-3 deep for 50 blocks and reaches y55 only at ~x6148. It faces west, towards the station's jetty, 130 blocks off the deck. Rechecked by the tool on every build.
portal.protected_by_the_lane: tools/sea_life.py and tools/sea_floor.py exclude data/portals.json's portals from their writes, not this arch (they do not read this file). The arch is sited INSIDE the coldwater_crossing ferry lane, which sea_life excludes (data/sea_life.json exclusions.ferry_lane_half_width_blocks, 32, either side of the segment between the two landings), and the tool refuses any apron or click column more than 28 from that segment. If the line or the lane width ever moves, the build fails rather than the kelp growing through the arch. When the arch moves into data/portals.json (hook), sea_life excludes it by itself.

buoy.why: the station's marker over the arch, what the telescope is trained on: a red float at the sea's level (the deck rule, data/sea_town.json: a block AT the level replaces the top water layer) and a lantern on it. Neither is a spawn condition (checked by the tool).

hook.sealed_message: The arch is cold and dark, and the sheet will not give. Something beyond it is very large, and asleep.
hook.flag: NONE YET. The cave's opening condition (a badge, a story flag, the champion) is the owner's to choose; it is checked in the destination function when the cave exists.

ferry.why: The 'ferry guy' the owner asked for is the station jetty's ferryman, a stop on a new line of the existing ferry system (data/ferries.json lines coldwater_crossing): the jetty is built by tools/ferry_docks.py at R16H and the ferrymen are placed by tools/ferries.py at R17F, so this pack builds neither. The far end is Northlight's existing landing on South Pine Isle (built 2026-09-30), whose packet master then offers both crossings: a second landing on the same island's coast would be a second jetty and a second ferryman for no new destination. Fare and gate are the Northlight packet's ($400, Koga's badge): a cheaper or ungated boat to the same island would undo the packet's gate.

blocks.rule: vanilla 1.21.1 only, none a spawn condition in data/spawn_blocks.json (checked by the tool on every build; light blue wool and lightning rods are, and are not used). No chests (tools/portals_audit.py's Gimmighoul reading) and no beds (the blackout recovery owns respawn points): barrels and carpets, as at the Frostpeak camp.

the station's telescope, trained on the red buoy the researchers moored over the sealed arch on the sea floor

researchers.name: Dr. Ines Calder
researchers.greeting: Coldwater Station. Three of us, a hut, a telescope, and something on the sea floor that nobody can explain.

topics.says: The red buoy, bearing {arch_bearing}, about {arch_range} blocks out. We moored it over an arch on the sea floor, {arch_depth} blocks down. Old stone, a sheet of dark glass, and lamps that were lit before any of us were born.

topics.ask: What do you think it is?
topics.says: A door. The sea has a legend here: a great Pokemon that sleeps under the water and raised the oceans once, when the world was young. Kyogre. The fishermen say the arch is its door. I think they may be right, and I would very much like to be the one who proves it.
Nobody has. You'd need to know how to dive, and even then the arch won't open. It isn't locked the way a door is locked. It's waiting. When it opens, I want to know about it first.

Our boatman runs the launch to Northlight, on the Pine Isles, from the jetty below. It's the packet company's crossing, so it's their price and their rule: ${fare}, and only with {gate}. It doesn't go near the arch. Nothing does.

researchers.name: Tobin Rask
researchers.greeting: Shut the door, if you would. I've spent a season measuring one patch of sea, and it keeps giving me numbers I can't explain.

topics.says: Ice we cut from the water over the arch, in summer. The sea freezes right over it, in a ring, and nowhere else. Water that cold should sink. This rises.

That the sea was made, not found. A Pokemon that brings the rain and pushes the water up over the land, and sleeps when it is done. Every coast has a story like that. This is the only coast where the story has a door.
The water's deep and cold off the shelf, and a swimmer tires fast. Don't go out to the buoy without a partner that can dive.

researchers.name: Wren Moss
researchers.greeting: Mind the theodolite. That's Northlight's landing it's laid on: bearing {landing_bearing}, about {landing_range} blocks. The boat runs straight down that line.

topics.says: Two readings on the board: the buoy, bearing {arch_bearing}, and the landing, bearing {landing_bearing}. The arch sits right on the boat's line. Our boatman swears the water goes still when he passes over it.
Because of the arch. The jetty was the excuse, the boat pays for the coffee. Nobody comes out this way except the boat.

spawns.why: The station and the arch add no spawn table, no Habitat Block and no spawn-free zone. Marsh country's own tables cover the ground; the station is a lead, not an encounter.
